extracted.intended_audience: horror writers, HWA members, nominees, and others submitting or voting for Bram Stoker Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural criteria for recommending, submitting, nominating, and voting for works in the Bram Stoker Awards, including membership eligibility, jury/submission procedures, ballot rules, and nominee benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Works must fit one of the Bram Stoker Award categories to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work doesn’t fit in any of the categories, it cannot be eligible. The organization acknowledges the wide-ranging nature of horror but cannot cover everything within an award category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition regardless of HWA membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards are intended to recognize the best work every year across the horror genre, regardless of whether the author is a member of the organization or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-members may win, but other parts of the process (recommending, voting) are restricted to members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may recommend works
rubrics_metrics.description: Only HWA members can recommend works to be nominated for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are the mechanism that puts works in contention for nomination; a recommendation means someone enjoyed the work enough to put it forward, and if a work receives enough recommendations it can become a nominee. To make a recommendation, members must log into the Members Only area and use the 'RECOMMEND A WORK' form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may vote
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Active/Pro and Lifetime HWA members may vote on the Bram Stoker Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting eligibility also requires being in good standing (i.e., having renewed membership dues) by January 31st of the calendar year. Members who renew after that date are not eligible to vote for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership standing and ballot distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Active/Pro and Lifetime members in good standing as of January 31 receive the preliminary and final ballots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are eligible but did not receive a ballot, check your Spam folder and whitelist noreply@limesurvey.org. If still missing, contact opscomm@horror.org. Note Microsoft domains (Outlook/Hotmail/MSN) may reject LimeSurvey emails; contact opscomm for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstain question behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: When filling out the ballot, you do not need to click 'No' on the abstain question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The survey is coded so that no response to the abstain question is treated as a 'no' automatically. Only click the abstain question if you actually plan to abstain from the category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot finality and error correction
rubrics_metrics.description: When you submit your ballot, it is considered final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is an error in your ballot that needs to be rectified, reach out to opscomm@horror.org for assistance and provide screenshots as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to juries (Submittable) procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit work to a jury via Submittable, you will receive an auto-generated letter informing you the jury has received your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reach out to the jury afterward to check receipt. If you did not receive the auto-generated letter (and it's not in Spam), contact stokerchair@horror.org for assistance. If your work is chosen by the Jury, you will receive a special iMailer to promote your work before final voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Reading List vs Jury submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Works on the Recommended Reading List are solely those "recommended" by HWA members in a given year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Submittable submission to a jury is a separate process from member recommendations. Appearing on the Recommended List requires a member recommendation; being submitted to a jury does not automatically place a work on that list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury service eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Members can serve on the Bram Stoker Award juries depending on membership level, qualifications, and availability of open slots on a given jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serving on a jury is not automatic; selection considers membership category and the juror's qualifications relative to open positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination meaning and path
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommendation is not the same as being a nominee; if your work receives enough recommendations it can become a Bram Stoker Award nominee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations are the initial step; sufficient recommendations (per the awards' process) lead to nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominee benefits and publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees receive recognition and promotional materials but not free StokerCon entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominees receive a nomination certification hand-signed by the organization's President (suitable for framing), a listing on the Bram Stoker Awards website, the right to place an official nomination seal on the work, and eligibility to purchase discounted gala tickets. They do not receive complimentary StokerCon admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official seals and medallions
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners and nominees may obtain official seals/medallions for use on their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAQ provides links to download the seals or a zipped file of medallions for placement on nominated/winning works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark notice for award name
rubrics_metrics.description: The little 'R' in the circle next to the Bram Stoker Awards® indicates the name is trademarked by HWA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HWA attorneys will enforce the trademark against unauthorized use of the awards' name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find complete rules and additional guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Bram Stoker Awards rules are available as a PDF linked from the FAQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rules PDF still leaves questions, the FAQ suggests a LitReactor interview as additional pointers.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to check membership status (WildApricot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use WildApricot (View profile) to check membership level and billing status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WildApricot shows membership level (Individual, Corporate, or Family) and membership status (Active or TK) in billing info; private section shows User ID and membership Type (Ally, Affiliate, Active Pro, or Lifetime). Only Active Pro or Lifetime members who are in good standing as of January 31 are eligible to vote.
